title: Walter Koenig, Ensign Chekov on Star Trek: The Original Series, dead at 90
summary: Actor Walter Koenig, who played Ensign Pavel Chekov, the youthful Russian navigator on the Star Trek television series and several movies, has died. He was 90.

image.caption: Walter Koenig, seen here as he was honoured with a star on the Hollywood Walk of Fame on Sept. 10, 2012, died Monday at the age of 90, his talent agent said. (David Livingston/Getty Images)

blocks.text: Actor Walter Koenig, who played Ensign Pavel Chekov, the youthful Russian navigator on the Star Trek television series and several movies, has died. He was 90.
U.S. actor 'was a writer, a teacher, a thoughtful man and a loyal friend,' wrote co-star George Takei
Koenig died Monday at his home in the North Hollywood neighbourhood of Los Angeles, talent agent Zachery McGinnis said in a statement.

In Star Trek, Chekov was the sole Communist-bloc member of the starship Enterprise's bridge staff. His friendly, supportive presence showed how the rival nations (in the far-off future in which the show was set) were capable of working together.
Speaking heavily Russian-accented English, Chekov embodied stereotypical Russian personality traits, including fierce pride, love of poetry and blind loyalty.
Star Trek ran on NBC from 1966 to 1969 and has had an almost unprecedented afterlife as fans, or Trekkies, kept interest in the show alive.
"My heart is heavy," Koenig's castmate George Takei said in a post on social media. "Walter was more than Chekov. He was a writer, a teacher, a thoughtful man, and a loyal friend."
George Takei as Sulu, left, and Walter Koenig as Chekov are shown in an archival photo from the set of Star Trek: The Original Series. (Getty Images)

"Walter's legacy extends far beyond the screen. Through countless convention appearances and interactions with fans, he shared his kindness, wit, and appreciation with everyone fortunate enough to meet him. He understood what Star Trek meant to people and embraced the community that grew around it," McGinnis said. "Thank you, Walter, for the memories, the inspiration, and for boldly going where few have gone before."
McGinnis said Koenig died surrounded by his daughter and niece.
Koenig played Chekov in seven Star Trek movies starting in 1979, as well as innumerable other spinoffs, including writing a Star Trek book, Chekov's Enterprise, in 1980.
The TV show has also inspired multiple spinoff TV series, with new casts, and conventions that draw thousands of fans.
Koenig returned to the science-fiction genre with occasional appearances in the syndicated 1990s TV series Babylon 5.
